reading.p: The Book of Ephesians was written by St. Paul the Apostle around 60 to 62 AD, during his first imprisonment in Rome. For this reason it is counted among the Prison Epistles. Paul addresses the local Church in Ephesus, but the letter is also an encyclical, a universal message to the whole Body of Christ throughout the ages.
Ephesians may be read as an icon of the New Creation. Its purposes are several:

list: The Ontological Unity: to reveal the Church not merely as a group, but as the fullness of Christ, His living Body and the Holy Temple where God dwells.
The Reconciliation: to proclaim the Mystery hidden from ages, that Jews and Gentiles are joined into One New Humanity, destroying the middle wall of partition.
The Liturgical Life: to instruct the baptized in the Way of Holiness, transitioning from the old man to the new man in Christ.
The Ascetic Struggle: to equip the faithful for Spiritual Warfare, providing the Armor of God to stand firm against the powers of darkness.

reading.p: The central revelation of Ephesians is the Church. The letter is not about individual spirituality alone, but about the mystery of Christ and His Body. In the Oriental Orthodox understanding, the Church is a living reality, not merely an idea. Christ is the Head, and the Church is His Body.

reading.quote: And hath put all things under his feet, and gave him to be the head over all things to the church, Which is his body, the fulness of him that filleth all in all.

reading.h2: The Church as Body and Bride

reading.p: Paul uses theophanic images to show that salvation is a communal reality, not a private one. A theophany is a God-showing. When we say an image is theophanic, we mean it is not just a metaphor or a pretty picture; it is a description of how God's Uncreated Light and presence break into our world.
The Church is the fullness of Christ. As a body cannot live without a head, and a head is not complete without its members, Christ chooses to be completed by us.
This is the Great Mystery. It reveals that the goal of human life is a Sacramental Union. Just as a husband and wife become one flesh, the Church becomes one spirit with Christ.

reading.quote: For the husband is the head of the wife, even as Christ is the head of the church: and he is the saviour of the body.

reading.h2: The Body and the Head: Organic Unity

reading.p: We often think of the Body as a metaphor for teamwork, but the biblical context is more organic and vital.

list: Life-Source: a body without a head is a corpse. By calling Christ the Head, Paul is saying that the Church's very life, direction, and nervous system come from Him.
Interdependence: in a body, a toe cannot claim to be independent of the lungs. This shatters the idea of private Christianity; if one part of the body suffers, the whole system feels the stress.

The Fullness: Ephesians 1:23 calls the Church the fullness of Him who fills all in all, which suggests that Christ chooses to manifest His presence on earth through this collective group, rather than appearing as a solo actor.

reading.h2: The Bride and the Bridegroom: Covenantal Intimacy

reading.p: If the Body emphasizes unity and function, the Bride emphasizes love and identity. Paul points out that Christ gave Himself up for the Bride (Ephesians 5:25). This moves salvation away from a legal transaction and into the realm of a marriage covenant.

The text describes Christ washing the Bride with the word to present her without stain or wrinkle. This shows that the Church's holiness is not a do-it-yourself project; it is the result of Christ's ongoing care for His people as a whole. Paul explicitly says that human marriage is a signpost pointing toward this deeper reality: the ultimate goal of history is the union of the Creator with His creation.

reading.quote: Husbands, love your wives, even as Christ also loved the church, and gave himself for it;

reading.p: God's plan is to gather all things into Christ, and the Church is the visible sign of that gathering. Salvation is not only forgiveness; salvation is new creation, union, and a new humanity in Christ.

reading.quote: That in the dispensation of the fulness of times he might gather together in one all things in Christ, both which are in heaven, and which are on earth; even in him:

reading.p: Ephesians teaches grace clearly, saying, 'By grace you have been saved' (Ephesians 2:8). In the Oriental Orthodox understanding, grace is God's life and power given to heal and transform us. Grace does not cancel obedience; it creates and empowers it. So in Ephesians 2:8-10 grace leads us to be created for good works, and in Ephesians 1:4 we are called to be holy.

list: Chapters 1-3 (Identity): what God has done in Christ.
Chapters 4-5 (Life): how the Church must live.
Chapter 6 (Spiritual Warfare): how believers stand and endure.

reading.p: Before St. Paul gives a single command, he spends three chapters explaining what God has already finished. The theology is that you are adopted, redeemed, and sealed. The shift is that we move from being dead in trespasses to being seated in heavenly places. The goal is to understand that the Church is not a human invention, but a divine mystery revealed.

reading.quote: I therefore... beseech you that ye walk worthy of the vocation wherewith ye are called.

reading.p: The word 'therefore' is the hinge of the whole letter. Because of who you are, as described in Chapters 1-3, this is how you must live, as described in Chapters 4-5. This is not about getting saved; it is about walking out the salvation you already have. It covers unity, purity, and the Body and Bride relationships in the home and the church.

reading.quote: Finally, my brethren, be strong in the Lord... Put on the whole armour of God.

reading.p: A worthy walk inevitably triggers opposition. Notice that the armor is mostly defensive. The goal is not to win a new victory, since Christ already won it in Chapter 1, but to stand and hold the ground that Christ has already won.
Paul names the spiritual blessings God has given us:
The key idea is this: your identity is not your past. Your identity is Christ.

reading.quote: According as he hath chosen us in him before the foundation of the world, that we should be holy and without blame before him in love:
In whom we have redemption through his blood, the forgiveness of sins, according to the riches of his grace;

In whom ye also trusted, after that ye heard the word of truth, the gospel of your salvation: in whom also after that ye believed, ye were sealed with that holy Spirit of promise, Which is the earnest of our inheritance until the redemption of the purchased possession, unto the praise of his glory.

reading.p: St. Paul prays that the Church may receive the Spirit of Wisdom and Revelation, so as to know God not as a concept, but through a living relationship. He prays for the enlightened eyes of the heart, that we may perceive our Hope, which is our calling, our Inheritance, which is the Kingdom, and the Power of the Resurrection.

reading.quote: That the God of our Lord Jesus Christ, the Father of glory, may give unto you the spirit of wisdom and revelation in the knowledge of him: The eyes of your understanding being enlightened; that ye may know what is the hope of his calling, and what the riches of the glory of his inheritance in the saints, And what is the exceeding greatness of his power to us-ward who believe, according to the working of his mighty power,

reading.h3: The Orthodox Way: Prayer over Pride

reading.p: In the Orthodox way of knowing, theology is not a trophy for the proud; it is a gift received through prayer and humility. Theology is doxology. As the Desert Fathers taught, if you are a theologian you will pray truly, and if you pray truly you are a theologian. Knowledge without prayer leads to pride. Revelation is a gift received on one's knees, not a trophy won by the intellect.

studyGuide.overview: Ephesians, one of St. Paul's Prison Epistles, is an encyclical revealing the Church as the living Body and Bride of Christ, the fullness of Him who fills all in all. It teaches that salvation is not only forgiveness but new creation and union, gathering Jew and Gentile into one new humanity, and it moves from identity (who we are in Christ) to life (how we walk) to endurance (standing firm in spiritual warfare).
keyPoints: The central revelation of Ephesians is the Church, a living reality with Christ as Head and the faithful as His Body.
The Body and Bride images are theophanic, showing salvation as communal and as a sacramental union with Christ.
Salvation is new creation, union, and a new humanity, not forgiveness alone; God gathers all things into Christ.
Grace is God's life and power that heals and transforms; it does not cancel obedience but creates and empowers it.
The structure hinges on 'therefore' in 4:1: because of who we are (Ch. 1-3), this is how we must walk (Ch. 4-5), standing firm in warfare (Ch. 6).
Our identity is not our past but Christ: chosen, adopted, redeemed, and sealed with the Holy Spirit.
True theology is received through prayer and humility, on one's knees, not won by intellect.
reviewQuestions: Why is Ephesians called both a local letter and an encyclical, and what does that mean for us today?
What is the central revelation of Ephesians, and how does the Oriental Orthodox tradition describe the Church?
Explain the difference in emphasis between the Body image and the Bride image of the Church.
What does it mean that salvation is new creation and union, not forgiveness alone?
How does the word 'therefore' in Ephesians 4:1 hold the whole letter together?
How is grace understood in the Orthodox sense, and how does it relate to obedience and good works?
Why is theology described as a gift received through prayer rather than a trophy won by intellect?

checks: The Church is presented as the living Body and Bride of Christ, a real ecclesial reality, consistent with Tewahedo ecclesiology.
Grace is described as God's uncreated life and power that heals and transforms, empowering obedience rather than canceling it (synergy upheld).
Salvation is framed as new creation, union, and Theosis-oriented transformation, not mere legal forgiveness.
Marriage is named as a signpost to the sacramental union of Christ and the Church, consistent with the Mystery of Matrimony.
Theology as prayerful doxology, received in humility, reflects the patristic and Orthodox way of knowing.
